description:
Follow-up to auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement. `scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py`
`compare_ruleset` (lines 135-180) already compares the develop ruleset's
enforcement state, target ref, required status checks, strict-check policy,
required_linear_history, non_fast_forward, deletion, and bypass actors — but
it never inspects the ruleset's `pull_request` rule (required_approving_review_count,
require_code_owner_review). So the daily `release-canary.yml` ruleset-drift job
(and the validate-main-pr.yml bootstrap invocation) can stay green forever even
while the develop ruleset still shows required_approving_review_count: 0 and
require_code_owner_review: false — the documented live state in
docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md:119-121.

The review-rule predicate already exists and is correct:
`_project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py` (`review_enforcement_findings`)
reads `SOUNDNESS_PREFIXES` from `_project/scripts/auto_merge_soundness_paths.py`
so its narration cannot drift from the auto-merge withholding set. But today it
only runs (a) manually, piped from `gh api repos/.../rules/branches/develop`, or
(b) as a pinned-logic unit test in `tests/unit/release/test_ruleset_review_enforcement.py`
that exercises fixture JSON, not the live ruleset. Nothing wires it into the
daily canary that already has ruleset-read (`RULESET_DRIFT_TOKEN`) access. That
means the admin-enforcement TODO's w3 verification step ("meta-check turns red
if the ruleset enforcement is ever removed") is not actually automated at the
canary layer — only the one-time manual verify command in the runbook covers it.

anti_patterns.dont: flip the canary to enforcing without first checking whether the admin PUT from auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement has actually landed
anti_patterns.why: that repeats the same 'code says enforced, repo layer does not' gap this whole line of TODOs exists to close.

anti_patterns.dont: reimplement required_approving_review_count / require_code_owner_review logic inline in ruleset_drift_check.py
anti_patterns.why: import review_enforcement_findings from _project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py so the two scripts cannot drift apart.

preserves.behavior: The RELEASE_READINESS_OVERRIDE_SHA/_REASON emergency override in ruleset_drift_check.py continues to short-circuit before any new check runs.

_project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py remains the single source of truth for the review-rule predicate; ruleset_drift_check.py imports it rather than duplicating the required_approving_review_count / require_code_owner_review checks.

scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py's existing comparisons (required checks, strict policy, linear history, non-fast-forward, deletion, bypass actors, target refs) are unchanged for both develop-squash-only and main-release-only.

prior_art.concept: _project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py:review_enforcement_findings — the single source of truth for the review-rule predicate; import it, do not reimplement the required_approving_review_count / require_code_owner_review checks inline in ruleset_drift_check.py.
scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py:compare_ruleset — reuse this comparison-and-findings pattern; add one more section rather than a parallel mechanism.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/release/ -k ruleset_review_enforcement -q
verifications.description: ruleset_review_enforcement's own pinned test still passes

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/release/ -k ruleset_drift -q
verifications.description: ruleset_drift_check now flags a fixture develop ruleset with required_approving_review_count=0
verifications.expected: new/updated test asserts a review-enforcement finding is present when the fixture ruleset lacks review requirements

work_units.notes:
If ruleset_drift_check.py starts asserting required_approving_review_count>=1
and require_code_owner_review=true immediately, the daily canary goes
permanently red until the admin action in auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement
is applied (live state is currently 0/false per
docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md:119-121). Two options: (a) land this
only after the admin PUT is confirmed applied (this item stays blocked on
that TODO's w3), or (b) land a warn-only mode now (findings printed, exit 0)
that flips to enforcing once the admin action lands. Record the decision
here and in the PR description; do not silently pick one.
work_units.summary: Decide sequencing: land review-rule drift coverage before or after the admin PUT lands

work_units.notes:
Add a call to `review_enforcement_findings` (from
_project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py) inside or alongside
`compare_ruleset` for the develop-squash-only ruleset only (main-release-only
has no equivalent requirement documented). Reuse `extract_rules` to normalize
the already-fetched live ruleset payload — do not re-fetch. Append its
findings to the existing findings list so `render_summary` and the JSON
`--output` payload surface them the same way as other drift findings.
work_units.summary: Import ruleset_review_enforcement's predicate into ruleset_drift_check.py's compare_ruleset

work_units.notes:
Update docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md's "Ruleset drift is checked
by scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py" paragraph to say it now also asserts
review enforcement for develop, and update or retire the now-partially-
redundant "Verify (manual or release-canary...)" command if the canary
covers it automatically. Confirm release-canary.yml (~line 160) and
validate-main-pr.yml (~line 115) both still pass the token/env this needs
and that a failure renders clearly in their job summaries (same pattern as
existing drift findings).
work_units.summary: Update the runbook and confirm both CI call sites surface the new failure mode

work_units.notes:
Add a fixture-based test (alongside tests/unit/release/test_ruleset_drift_check.py
if it exists, else tests/unit/release/) asserting compare_ruleset now flags a
develop ruleset missing review enforcement, and stays silent on that axis
once the fixture has required_approving_review_count>=1 and
require_code_owner_review=true. Keep tests/unit/release/test_ruleset_review_enforcement.py
passing unchanged — this item extends the drift checker, not the predicate.
work_units.summary: Extend or add unit coverage for the merged drift+review-enforcement path
